problem: The caption says the dashed static bypass is used "for maintenance or if the inverter trips". Section 1 and quiz Q6 correctly separate the two: a static bypass (thyristors) takes the load to mains on inverter overload or fault, while a maintenance bypass is a separate manual path that isolates the UPS for service. The caption contradicts the chapter's own definition.
fix: The dashed static bypass carries the load straight from mains if the inverter trips or is overloaded. Servicing uses a separate maintenance bypass that isolates the whole UPS.

problem: Transfer time is given only for the off-line type. A line-interactive UPS also transfers the load to its inverter on mains failure; not stating this leaves the reader thinking only the standby type switches.
fix: Add: a line-interactive UPS also switches the load to the inverter on mains failure, with a transfer time of a few milliseconds, shorter than the off-line type because the inverter is already running and regulating.

problem: "Output THD is the RMS sum of harmonic voltages" is loose wording; a student may read it as adding the harmonic RMS values directly instead of the square root of the sum of squares.
fix: Output THD = √(V₂² + V₃² + V₄² + …) ÷ V₁ × 100%, where V₁ is the fundamental RMS voltage and V₂, V₃, … are the harmonic RMS voltages.

problem: The linear-supply and SMPS description repeats material that belongs to the power-supplies unit, and the two cross-references ("see Unit 3", "see 6.6") are plain text rather than links, so a phone reader cannot jump to them.
fix: Cut the linear-supply and SMPS basics to one sentence each, keeping only the crest-factor consequence for UPS sizing, and make the cross-references links to the relevant chapters.
